issues.description: Naming inconsistency for the code area where the position calculation should be placed: the problem statement refers to inserting code in the 'calculate_position' area (and instructs students accordingly), while the template uses the comment/label 'calculate_offset' for the third TODO. The solution implements the calculation inline in main near a TODO labeled 'calculate position'. This inconsistent naming may confuse students about exactly where to place their code and which TODO to use.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to 'calculate_offset' (matching the template) or change the template TODO/comment to 'calculate_position' (matching the problem statement). Ensure the solution and template use the same label/text so students unambiguously know where to implement the code.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to insert assembler code in the area named 'calculate_position', but the template's corresponding TODO comment uses the name 'calculate_offset' while the solution uses the phrase 'calculate position'. These three different identifiers (calculate_position, calculate_offset, calculate position) refer to the same conceptual task (compute the pixel memory address) but are named inconsistently across artifacts. This may confuse students about where exactly to place their code or which comment/label the problem text refers to.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single, consistent name for the address-calculation region across all artifacts. For example, rename the template comment and any labels to 'calculate_position' (or update the problem statement to 'calculate_offset' if preferred). Also add an explicit labeled region or comment in the template (e.g., 'calculate_position: ; TODO') so students can unambiguously find where to insert the code.
